normalized_evidence.raw_content: General anesthesia. Right breast-conserving surgery for breast cancer + sentinel lymph node biopsy + fascial tissue flap reconstruction [breast conservation + sentinel lymph node]. The patient was placed supine with both upper extremities abducted. After induction of anesthesia, the surgical field was disinfected and draped. 5ml methylene blue was injected into the right areolar region, followed by massage for 5 minutes. A No. 10 blade was used to make a curved right axillary incision approximately 5cm in length. The skin and subcutaneous fat were divided layer by layer with electrocautery to enter the axilla. The first-echelon blue-stained lymph node was identified by following the blue-stained axillary lymphatic vessels, excised, and submitted for intraoperative frozen-section examination. The results showed: “Right axillary para-sentinel lymph node 1”: no metastatic carcinoma was identified in the lymph node on frozen section. “Right axillary para-sentinel lymph node 2”: macrometastatic carcinoma was identified in 1/1 lymph nodes on frozen section. “Right axillary para-sentinel lymph node 3”: no metastatic carcinoma was identified in the lymph node on frozen section. “Right axillary para-sentinel lymph node 4”: no metastatic carcinoma was identified in the lymph node on frozen section. “Right axillary sentinel lymph node 1”: no metastatic carcinoma was identified in the lymph node on frozen section. “Right axillary sentinel lymph node 2”: no metastatic carcinoma was identified in the lymph node on frozen section. “Right axillary sentinel lymph node 3”: no metastatic carcinoma was identified in the lymph node on frozen section. “Right axillary sentinel lymph node 4”: no metastatic carcinoma was identified in the lymph node on frozen section. Right breast-conserving surgery for breast cancer was then performed. An incision approximately 5 cm long was made through the skin and subcutaneous tissue. The edge of the skin flap was elevated, and electrocautery was used to perform undermining dissection between the subcutaneous fat and glandular tissue. The mass and more than 2cm of the surrounding breast tissue were widely excised down to the pectoralis major fascia, with partial excision of the pectoralis major fascia. Sutures and titanium clips were used to mark each margin of the specimen. Intraoperative mammography confirmed complete excision of the mass. The margins were submitted for frozen-section pathological examination, which showed that the suture-marked “superior, medial, inferior, and lateral margins” of the “right breast-conserving specimen” were all free of carcinoma. The margins were negative. Meticulous hemostasis was achieved. After placement of titanium clips, fascial tissue around the residual cavity was mobilized and transferred as a tissue flap for reconstruction. 2-0 silk sutures were used for ligation and fixation. The residual cavity and subcutaneous layer were closed with interrupted 4-0 silk sutures, and the skin was closed with a continuous intradermal suture using 4-0 slowly absorbable Vicryl. The procedure was completed. Postoperatively, the wound was dressed with a compressive chest band, and routine fluid replacement and supportive treatment were provided. Vital signs were closely monitored, with attention to any active bleeding or oozing from the wound.
